messages:
tara-support: FYI customer ACME escalated — sudden p95/p99 regressions after last weekend deploy, lots of slow tails (~1s p95 from ~120ms). They reported intermittent 502s too. sending logs.
liz-eng-runtime: can you paste repro + a sample request? which route/model? any tenant-level traffic spike?

tara-support: route = /v1/generate (gpt-3-like), model pinned, customer on Dedicated cluster eu-west-1. No big QPS change. Attached request example: curl with a bunch of headers and dynamic session cookie.

tara-support: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-..."
  -H "X-Client-Version: 1.12.4"
  -H "X-Feature-Flag: true"
  -H "Cookie: sess=abc123; other=1"
  -d '{"prompt":"hi","userId":"u-258","session":"s-987"}'
```

mike-sre: looking at infra metrics — big spike in `prefix_cache_miss_rate` and `kv_evictions/sec` around 2025-11-07T09:20Z. p95/p99 correlate with eviction churn. CPU ops on inference nodes unchanged, so likely cache warmup thrash.

liz-eng-runtime: can you dump a few cache keys from the node? suspecting we have header/cookie leakage into the prefix key. if keys blow up cardinality will evict hot prefixes.

tara-support: pasted sample keys (sanitized):
```
model:gpt3:/v1/generate:client=web:user=u-258:cookie=sess=abc123
model:gpt3:/v1/generate:client=web:user=u-258:cookie=sess=def456
model:gpt3:/v1/generate:client=mobile:user=u-258:cookie=sess=ghi789
```

liz-eng-runtime: yep — cache key currently includes raw cookie and `X-Client-Version` in some code paths. that's high cardinality. code: 
```
function makePrefixKey(req){
  return `${model}:${route}:client=${req.headers['x-client']}:user=${req.body.userId}:cookie=${req.headers.cookie}`
}
```

ashley-eng: oof. that's the bug we thought we fixed last quarter. looks like a new handler was added (analytics middleware) and it constructs keys differently.

ron-product: severity? customer impacted SLA? do we need to roll back?

tara-support: ACME seeing user-facing latency and occasional 502s. They opened an urgent ticket, on a 24h enterprise SLA.

liz-eng-runtime: proposed mitigations (short):
- hotfix: normalize cache key construction to drop cookies/session ids + whitelist low-cardinality headers. small patch to handler. (PR -> canary -> 10% -> 100%)
- temporary operational: disable prefix caching on that route for the tenant (feature flag) to stop thrash while we fix. cheaper than rollback.
- backend: increase KV cache size on the dedicated shard as emergency (buy time) — ops only if safe.
- longer term: add key-normalization lint + unit tests + a prefix-key-entropy alarm.

mike-sre: ops playbook notes: when eviction/sec > X and miss_rate > Y, flip `prefix_cache_enabled=false` for tenant, and kick an async backfill to warm the canonical keys. also add a short circuit to avoid writing keys with >50 chars of unknown header payload.

tara-support: can we do hotfix now? customer is pacing.

deploy-bot: build 3896 passed CI, staging deploy queued.

liz-eng-runtime: I'll open a tiny PR to remove cookies and `x-client-version` from keys and add normalization. will add a toggle to short-circuit if header value length > 32.

ashley-eng: i can do the tenant feature-flag disable now — patching the routing policy, will monitor.

mike-sre: ops will also bump the dedicated shard cache TTLs and monitor `kv_warmup_ops` so we don't overload the backend.

ron-product: timeline & owners? customer update in 30m.

liz-eng-runtime: PR #4821 in review, aim for canary in 15m, full roll in 45m if metrics look good. I'll handle the PR + canary.
ashley-eng: feature flag off in 5m, I'll update ticket and slack.
mike-sre: i'll watch metrics and rollback plan ready.

tara-support: sending ACME a note: "we found excessive cache key cardinality caused by cookies in keys; applying temporary flag and a short fix now, expect improvement within ~15-45m" :thumbsup:

liz-eng-runtime: followups (post-mitigation):
- add automated test that fails build if new key includes any header in `denylist_headers` or any `cookie` content
- emit `prefix_key_entropy` metric and a pager when > threshold
- run a one-off canonicalization job to backfill normalized keys and pre-warm top prefixes for the tenant

ron-product: add this to postmortem if customer still impacted — want clear RCAs and timeline.

tara-support: will update ticket with timeline and owners. thanks team.

liz-eng-runtime: quick note: if we need immediate relief and canary is slow, we can also enable a lightweight per-route LRU guard that rejects writes for keys with >N unique fragments for 1 minute. saves eviction storms.

mike-sre: agreed. monitoring checklists in place. ping me on pager if latency creeps back up.

deploy-bot: deploy canary -> prod rollout started by liz-eng-runtime at 1718504560

liz-eng-runtime: canary metrics look good so far, p95 trending down from 1.2s -> 160ms, kv_evictions/sec dropping. rolling to 25%.

tara-support: ACME confirmed improvement on their side, latency back to normal, still watching for 502s.

ron-product: great. postmortem + followups scheduled. thanks everyone.

liz-eng-runtime: filing a short retro and a small RFC for key-normalization linter.

ashley-eng: closing tenant feature-flag; keeping monitoring for 24h.

tara-support: closing thread with update to customer. :white_check_mark:
